Go to slide 1 out of 5 Go to slide 2 out of 5 Go to slide 3 out of 5 Go to slide 4 out of 5 Go to slide 5 out of 5 Overview Most gallbladder surgery today is done using laparoscopic surgical techniques, in which narrow instruments, including a camera, are introduced into the abdomen through small puncture holes. If the procedure is expected to be straightforward, laparoscopic cholecystectomy may be used. A laparoscopic camera is inserted into the abdomen near the umbilicus (navel). Instruments are inserted through 2 more small puncture holes. The gallbladder is found, the vessels and tubes are cut, and the gallbladder is removed. Review Date 9/9/2023 Updated by: Debra G.
